analysis.investment_thesis: Clear Secured is a low-margin, capital-intensive facility management company with no discernible moat, burning cash at an accelerating rate (-₹26 Cr FCF in FY25) while piling on debt. Accounting profits are an illusion — the business destroys cash even as revenues grow.
key_strengths: Revenue growing 35%+ YoY (₹309→₹476 Cr), suggesting contract wins
ROCE of 20.4% looks acceptable on the surface
High promoter holding (73%) indicates skin in the game
key_risks: FCF deeply negative and worsening: -₹3 → -₹7 → -₹26 Cr; only 1/3 years OCF-positive
Debt exploded from ₹53 Cr to ₹128 Cr in one year; Debt/EBITDA = 3.9x (above my 2.5x limit)
Net profit FELL from ₹12→₹10 Cr despite 37% revenue growth — finance costs tripled (₹4→₹10 Cr), eating the business alive
red_flags: FCF/Net Income deeply negative (-260%) — accounting profits are not real cash earnings
Borrowings up 141% YoY (₹53→₹128 Cr); CWIP up 175% (₹8→₹22 Cr) — growth funded entirely by debt
Other income swung from +₹3 Cr to -₹2 Cr — possible write-offs or treasury losses
ROIC ≈ 8-9% (NOPAT ~₹23 Cr / invested capital ~₹264 Cr) — well below my 15% minimum threshold
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Invert first: what makes this a terrible business? Facility management is a commodity — contracts are won on price, clients switch freely, and there is no switching cost. EBITDA margins are 6-7% with net margins below 3%. The business cannot grow without consuming enormous capital, evidenced by assets nearly doubling (₹170→₹327 Cr) in a single year while net profit shrank. The gap between reported net income (₹10 Cr) and free cash flow (-₹26 Cr) — a ₹36 Cr divergence — is the most damning number in this entire data set. When a business consistently fails to convert earnings into cash, I want nothing to do with it.

The balance sheet is deteriorating rapidly. Debt tripling in a year to fund working capital and CWIP in a services business is a serious warning sign. At ₹128 Cr borrowings against ₹33 Cr EBITDA, debt service is consuming the marginal economics of growth — finance costs already jumped from ₹4 Cr to ₹10 Cr, directly suppressing net profit despite strong topline growth. The P/E of 18.8x is expensive for a business of this quality; on an EV/EBITDA basis (~11x), the market is pricing this as if it had durable advantages it simply does not possess. A poor business, in debt, burning cash, with no moat — I would not own this at any price near current levels.
